name: JSON.stringify()
description: Converts a JavaScript value into a JSON string, optionally filtering properties and pretty-printing with indentation.
parameters: value — the value to serialize. replacer — optional function or array to filter properties. space — optional indentation for pretty-printing.
notes: Functions, undefined values, and symbols are silently dropped or omitted during serialization.

name: JSON.parse()
description: Parses a JSON string, constructing the JavaScript value or object it describes.
parameters: text — the JSON string to parse. reviver — optional function to transform parsed values.
returns: The JavaScript value corresponding to the parsed JSON text.
notes: Throws a SyntaxError on malformed JSON — wrap in try...catch when parsing untrusted input.

name: Math.random()
description: Returns a pseudo-random floating-point number in the range [0, 1), including 0 but excluding 1.
notes: Not cryptographically secure — use the Web Crypto API's crypto.getRandomValues() for security-sensitive randomness.

name: Math.floor()
description: Rounds a number down to the nearest integer.
parameters: number — the value to round down.
returns: The largest integer less than or equal to the given number.

name: Math.round()
description: Rounds a number to the nearest integer, rounding .5 values up.

name: Math.max()
description: Returns the largest of the given numbers.
returns: The largest value, or -Infinity if no arguments are given.
notes: Use the spread operator to apply it to an array: Math.max(...array).

name: Math.min()
description: Returns the smallest of the given numbers.
returns: The smallest value, or Infinity if no arguments are given.

name: Math.abs()
description: Returns the absolute (non-negative) value of a number.

name: Number.isInteger()
description: Determines whether the given value is an integer, without coercing the input type.
returns: true if the value is a number and an integer, otherwise false.
example:
Number.isInteger(5); // true
Number.isInteger(5.5); // false
Number.isInteger('5'); // false
notes: Unlike the global isInteger-style checks, this does not coerce strings — '5' is not considered an integer.

name: Number.parseFloat()
description: Parses a string and returns a floating-point number, reading as much of the string as looks like a valid number.
returns: The parsed floating-point number, or NaN if the string cannot be parsed.
notes: Equivalent to the global parseFloat() function, but namespaced under Number for module-style consistency.

name: console.log()
description: Outputs one or more values to the console, commonly used for debugging.
parameters: value1, value2, ... — any values to print.
notes: Supports string substitution with %s, %d, %o and CSS styling with %c.

name: console.table()
description: Displays tabular data (an array of objects or a 2D structure) as a formatted table in the console.
parameters: data — an array or object to render as a table.
notes: Much easier to scan than console.log() for arrays of similarly-shaped objects.

name: setTimeout()
description: Schedules a function to run once after a specified delay, without blocking the rest of the program.
parameters: callback — function to execute. delayMs — delay in milliseconds. args — optional arguments passed to callback.
returns: A timeout ID that can be passed to clearTimeout().
notes: The delay is a minimum, not a guarantee — actual execution can be delayed further by the event loop's workload.

name: setInterval()
description: Repeatedly calls a function with a fixed time delay between each call, until cleared.
parameters: callback — function to execute repeatedly. intervalMs — delay between calls in milliseconds. args — optional arguments passed to callback.
returns: An interval ID that can be passed to clearInterval().
notes: Always store the returned ID so the interval can be stopped later — forgetting to clear it is a common source of memory leaks.

name: clearTimeout()
description: Cancels a timeout previously scheduled with setTimeout(), preventing its callback from running.
parameters: timeoutId — the ID returned by setTimeout().
example: const id = setTimeout(doThing, 5000); clearTimeout(id); // doThing never runs
notes: Also works to cancel a setInterval() timer via its interval-ID counterpart, clearInterval().
